title: Extracellular vesicle separation from milk and infant milk formula using acid precipitation and ultracentrifugation
protocol: Mix 4.4 g of IMF powder with 30 mL of warm, filtered water that has been boiled and cooled naturally.
Centrifuge 50 mL of SM or reconstituted IMF at 2,000 g for 20 min at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant carefully after centrifugation.
Discard the pellet containing any fat globules or debris.
If non-defatted milk is used as a starting material, centrifuge milk at 6,000 g for 10 min at 4°C to remove fats.
Proceed with the supernatant from the previous step and centrifuge again at 2,000 g for 20 min at 4°C.
Fold the WhatmanTM Grade 1 filter paper in half.
Fold the filter paper again to form a 90° center angle.
Place the folded filter paper on one side of the glass funnel.
Open one layer of the filter paper on the other side to form a funnel.
Carefully pour the supernatant through the funnel and collect the filtrate in a fresh tube at the bottom of the funnel.
Designate the filtrate obtained from untreated SM as SM_NT.
Designate the filtrate obtained from untreated IMF as IMF_NT.
Adjust the pH of milk to 4.6 using 6 N acetic acid drop-by-drop while stirring continuously.
Measure the pH of milk continuously during adjustment.
Allow the adjusted milk sample to sit for 10 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Centrifuge the sample at 5,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Mix equal volumes of diluent with SM samples.
Adjust pH to 4.6 using 6 N HCl for SM samples.
Place adjusted pH SM on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge SM at 5,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Filter the whey from SM as described above.
Mix equal volumes of diluent with IMF samples.
Adjust pH to 4.6 using 6 N HCl for IMF samples.
Place adjusted pH IMF on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge IMF at 5,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Filter the whey from IMF as described above.
Separate EVs by ultracentrifugation.
Mix 2.33 mL of sample with Optiprep to obtain a 40% solution for Gradient Ultracentrifugation (GUC).
Layer the 40% Optiprep solution at the bottom of a 17 mL tube, followed by layers of 30%, 20%, and 10% Optiprep solutions in PBS.
Add PBS on top of the layered solutions in the tube.
Ultracentrifuge the tube at 186,000 g for 18 hours at 4°C for GUC.
Load 38 mL of sample into a polypropylene tube for Differential Ultracentrifugation (DUC).
Centrifuge the tube at 12,000 g for 90 minutes at 4°C for DUC.
Centrifuge the tube again at 35,000 g for 90 minutes at 4°C for DUC.
Repeat centrifugation at 75,000 g for 90 minutes at 4°C for DUC.
Centrifuge the tube once more at 100,000 g for 90 minutes at 4°C for DUC.
Finally, centrifuge the tube at 200,000 g for 90 minutes at 4°C for DUC.
Collect the final pellet from the DUC process and store it for further use.
Store rotors at 4°C as per manufacturer’s suggestion.
Balance tubes using a microbalance to achieve the same weight ± 0.01 g/mL.
Perform gradient ultracentrifugation for 20 hours using an SW Type 32.1 Ti rotor in Optima XPN-100 Ultracentrifuge (Beckman Coulter, Brea, CA, USA).
Create a 40% (w/v) bottom layer by diluting 60% OptiPrep solution with each sample type.
Transfer the 7 ml of solution into the 17 ml polypropylene tube carefully in an upright position.
Place the tube at approximately 70° angle to form discontinuous gradient layers.
Layer the discontinuous gradient with 30% (w/v), 20% (w/v), 10% (w/v) and 5% (w/v) solutions of iodixanol from bottom to top, adding each layer drop by drop using a pipette.
Store prepared tubes at 4°C or on ice until all tubes are ready if preparing multiple gradient tubes.
Weigh rotor holders with a microbalance to balance all the tubes to the same weight ±0.01 g/mL.
Carefully place holders in pre-cooled rotor and set ultracentrifuge parameters according to software instructions.
Perform ultracentrifugation according to the specified parameters.
Collect 1 mL fractions after centrifugation; a total of 17 tubes corresponding to 17 mL volume.
Carefully collect each fraction from top to bottom using a P1000 pipette without disturbing the layers.
Zero the hand-held Pal-Ri Refractometer with distilled water.
Calibrate the refractometer and place 300 μL of each fraction on it for RI determination.
Record RI values to four decimal places.
Calculate density using the equation: Density = 3.3411 × RI – 3.4584.
Pool fractions based on densities into pool 1 (≤ 1.00 g/mL), pool 2 (1.10 to 1.20 g/mL), and pool 3 (≥ 1.20 g/mL).
After the pooling of fractions based on densities, add sterile PBS to bring the volume up to 38 mL.
Balance each tube to a similar weight ± 0.01 g/mL.
Place balanced tubes in a pre-cooled SW Type 32 Ti swinging bucket rotor.
Perform ultracentrifugation using specified parameters.
After centrifugation, carefully pipette out and discard all the liquid.
Resuspend the viscous pellet at the bottom with 1 mL of sterile PBS.
Store the resultant EV-enriched suspension at −80°C until further use.
Balance samples to their weight (± 0.01 g/mL difference).
Place balanced tubes into a pre-cooled SW Type 32 Ti swinging bucket rotor.
Perform ultracentrifugation using specified parameters.
Collect the pellet after each centrifugation step.
Resuspend the collected pellet in 1 mL PBS.
Store resuspended pellet at -80°C for potential further analysis.
Pour supernatant into a fresh tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant at the next speed setting.
